pages.hook: Many American fast restaurants let you build your own meal along a counter: you point, choose and the worker adds each layer. Learn the steps, in order, so you never freeze.
pages.polite: Choose one item at a time and say **please**. Say **No, thanks** or **No guacamole** if you do not want something.

mythfact.s: At a build-your-own bowl place, you choose each ingredient.
mythfact.why: The worker asks for rice, beans, toppings and sauce.

mythfact.s: The word “salsa” is Spanish for “sauce”.
Guacamole is always free at American restaurants.
Phoenix, Arizona, has very hot summers.
mythfact.why: Summer days there are often above 100°F (38°C).

mythfact.s: “Guacamole” is made mainly from tomatoes.

decode.q: How much is a chicken bowl with guacamole?
Which topping is NOT in this order?

compare.br: In Brazil, a “prato feito” or a self-service “por quilo” restaurant also lets you choose what goes on your plate.
compare.us: In the USA, you often go down a line and say each choice to the worker: protein, rice, beans, toppings.
compare.tip: Learn the order of the questions; the answers are one or two words.
compare.ask: What would you put in your perfect bowl? Say it in English.

quiz.q: Kai asks, “White rice or brown rice?” You say…
You do not want guacamole. You say…

quiz.why: That’s it = I don’t want anything else.

pages.title: Reading quest — How to build your bowl · part 1
text: Today, my friend Hector and I go to a bowl restaurant in **Phoenix**. The sun is hot, but the restaurant is cool. A man called Kai says, “Hi! **What kind of bowl?**”

**First**, choose a protein. I say, “**A chicken bowl, please.**” **Then**, Kai asks, “**White rice or brown rice?**” “Brown rice, with beans,” I say. **Next**, he asks about toppings. “**Salsa? Cheese? Guacamole?**” I say, “**Salsa and cheese. No guacamole.**”

**Finally**, Kai asks, “**Anything else?**” “No, **that’s it**. How much?” “Nine dollars,” he says. I pay, and he says, “**Enjoy your bowl!**” It looks so good. Hector says, “**That looks sick!**” and his bowl is full of everything.

pages.title: Reading quest — How to build your bowl · part 2
text: I love cooking shows. My favorite is “MasterChef Junior”, a show from 2013, where kids from eight to thirteen cook in a big kitchen. They use pots, pans and a stove. The judges say, “First, then, next, finally.” A bowl is a bit like a recipe too.
At home, you can build a bowl in four steps: first, rice; then, beans; next, toppings; finally, sauce. **Load it up**, and **dig in**!
